title: Palau and western Micronesia told to expect dry stretch ahead of El Nino
detail: Forecasters warned Palau and western Micronesia of a dry period before an expected El Nino, per a regional news report; no drought had been declared at the time.

title: Chinese research vessels cause alarm after repeated entries into Palau waters
detail: ABC reported that Palau was alarmed by repeated incursions of Chinese research vessels into its waters; Island Times separately reported Palau protesting unauthorized Chinese research-vessel activity in its EEZ.

title: Pacific Islands Forum opens in Palau under partner pressure
detail: PINA reported a packed agenda and pressure from outside partners as the 55th Pacific Islands Forum leaders meeting began in Koror, amid China-Taiwan tension over Taiwan's attendance.

title: Security, climate and drugs top Forum leaders agenda in Koror
detail: ABC described the Koror leaders meeting as politically charged, with security, climate change and drugs on the agenda.

title: Singapore foreign minister attends Forum meeting in Palau
detail: Singapore's MFA said Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan visited Palau for the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting on 31 August to 1 September 2026.

title: Palau described as focal point of US-China standoff
detail: Fortune reported that Palau, a country of about 18,000 people, had become ground zero for a US-China standoff as it hosted the Forum with Taiwan in attendance.

title: A third of Forum leaders absent from Palau meeting
detail: RFA reported that about a third of Forum leaders stayed away from the Palau meeting, which it described as less productive, against the backdrop of Taiwan-China tensions.

title: Forum outcomes in Koror mostly affirm existing positions
detail: A Devpolicy analysis said leaders in Koror largely affirmed, noted and endorsed existing positions rather than launching new initiatives.

title: US military buildup in Palau raises local fears of war
detail: A Manila Times (wire) report said the US military buildup in Palau, including radar and port projects, has stirred fears among residents that the islands could become a target in a conflict.
